sentences.text: Analyzing AC circuits with sine and cosine differential equations is extremely tedious.
By using Euler's formula: e^(j theta) = cos(theta) + j sin(theta), we transform time-domain sinusoids into complex vectors called Phasors.
A sinusoid v(t) = V_m cos(omega t + phi) becomes the phasor V = V_m ∠ phi.
In the phasor domain, resistors have impedance Z_R = R. Inductors have impedance Z_L = j omega L, where voltage leads current by 90 degrees.
Capacitors have impedance Z_C = 1 / (j omega C) = -j / (omega C), where current leads voltage by 90 degrees.
strong>The Classic Mnemonic 'ELI the ICE man': In an Inductor ($L$), Voltage ($E$) leads Current ($I$) $\\rightarrow$ ELI.
In a Capacitor ($C$), Current ($I$) leads Voltage ($E$) $\\rightarrow$ ICE.
